[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: L1 gold contexts uniformly report absolute oral bioavailability values or qualitative outcomes consistent with F >= 20% in humans for diverse lipophilic, basic, and heteroaromatic molecules; propylthiouracil, a thiourea-containing drug, has F 77 ± 13% (C02), and melperone, vernakalant, suvorexant, levofloxacin, BI 425809, phytoene, hyperforin, and pentazocine-in-cirrhosis all support F >= 20% (C01,C05,C14,C08,C11,C13,C07,C06,C04,C10,C12,C03,C09). None provides affirmative evidence of F < 20%.

L3 etamicastat, a cyclic-thiourea-containing molecule, shows measurable oral AUC after 200 mg with minimal food effect (C32,C42), supporting oral absorption and systemic exposure of thiourea-containing scaffolds.

L4 nepicastat, a close cyclic-thiourea analog, is highly permeable across Caco-2 and MDCK-II monolayers (Papp ~5.3-5.4 × 10^-5 cm/s; C89,C91,C119,C81,C129); lorcaserin, a small lipophilic basic chloroarene, is highly permeable with no P-gp substrate behavior (C94,C111,C100,C113,C127,C86,C126); domperidone absorption is virtually complete (C98,C128,C85); indapamide is 100% absorbed (C99); UC-781 is high permeability (C101). This supports favorable intestinal absorption for the query's lipophilic basic heteroaromatic scaffold.

L5 bidirectional transport for lorcaserin and loratadine shows high Papp with efflux ratios ~1.0-1.2, indicating no significant gut-wall efflux for similar lipophilic basic chloroarenes (C137,C150,C164,C179,C156,C133,C138,C131); domperidone and linezolid also show high permeability (C153,C146). Efflux examples such as GV196771, AFN-1252, and compound 1a are not query-related and do not constitute affirmative low-F evidence (C140,C152,C158,C136).

L6 hepatic clearance/metabolic stability evidence is mixed: lorcaserin, a similar lipophilic basic chloroarene, has low HLM CLint 18.57 µL/min/mg and is metabolized by multiple CYPs/FMO (C209,C180,C227); loratadine has HLM CLint 137 but human hepatocyte CLint 9.5-26.4 µL/min/10^6 cells and is orally bioavailable (C211,C205); prenylated flavonoids show moderate CYP metabolism (C224,C213,C225,C195,C223). PF-06282999, a thiouracil, has short rat liver microsomal half-life (C198,C183,C228) and FMO1 CLint 97.7 (C203), but this is a different thiouracil scaffold in rat microsomes and is outweighed by human F of propylthiouracil (C02) and high permeability of cyclic thiourea analogs. L6 does not provide affirmative threshold-relevant evidence of F < 20%.

Combined with uniformly high L1 gold-context F values and L3-L5 absorption/permeability/efflux evidence, F >= 20% remains better supported. L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.
